text:
alice: Heads-up — I spotted a repro where the console shows billing/project attribution switching to the org default when requests go through the authn-proxy exchange for service accounts. Seen it twice this morning in prod.
ben: hmm, can you paste the request headers / small trace? :eyes:
alice: minimal headers i captured: 
```
:authority: api.redwood.ai
authorization: Bearer sa-exchange-token
x-forwarded-for: 1.2.3.4
x-origin-project: project-123
x-origin-org: org-999
# after proxy run: x-effective-project: org-default
```
carol: ouch. is the quota system reading x-origin-project or x-effective-project? that determines billing.
dave: quota/ingestion currently prioritizes `x-effective-project` when present, fallback to `x-origin-project`. the proxy appears to be setting effective -> org default for some SA exchange paths.
ben: do we have telemetry for "auth.exchange.result.project" or similar? need to know how widespread.
dave: nope, we only log exchange-success bool + principal id. project tag not emitted at the moment (we only emit service_account_id and org_id).
alice: that explains it. UX hit: console shows project which matches billing and customers are confused.
carol: short term mitigation idea: console should show both "origin project" and "effective project" (like: Origin: project-123 · Effective: org-default) so users see what's being charged. low-risk UI change.
dave: agree. also add a metric tag on the auth-exchange span: `auth.exchange.project_attributed=<project|org-default|fallback>` so we can count how many flows attribute to org.
ben: for rollout: add a feature flag on console to toggle new column, then flip after 24h. telemetry flag on exchange service to start emitting the project tag at 5% sample.
carol: what about server-side policy: why is proxy deciding org-default? Is it because the SA doesn't have project-scoped binding?
dave: yes. proxy logic: if SA has no explicit project claim, we attach tenant-level (org-default) project to avoid orphaned requests. This is intentional for backcompat. But we should make it explicit in logs and console.
alice: can we change proxy to preserve x-origin-project when present (i.e., prefer explicit origin override) and only set effective when origin absent? That would reduce surprises.
dave: doable, but risk: some SA-exchange flows intentionally need org routing. Need to add a validation check: if x-origin-project present and exchange result grants permission to that project, keep it. otherwise fallback to org-default.
ben: sounds safe. let's do small steps: 1) console UI shows both values behind flag, 2) emit telemetry tag, 3) change proxy preserve-when-authorized behavior behind flag, 4) monitor metric and error/denial rate for 48h, 5) flip globally.
carol: agree. assign owners?
alice: I'll do the console change (UI + flag).
dave: I'll add telemetry and implement preserve-when-authorized in proxy behind a flag.
ben: I'll add dashboard: timeseries of `auth.exchange.project_attributed` broken down by reason (origin-kept, org-default, fallback-denied) and add alert if org-default > 10% for a customer cohort.
dave: deploy-bot: canary rollout for auth-proxy flag tomorrow at 09:00 UTC?
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: auth-proxy/preserve-origin-flag -> canary-1 (3 hosts) at 2026-03-24T09:00:00Z. I'll post updates in #release-war-room. :robot_face:
alice: quick note for docs: add short FAQ entry under authn/exchange that explains origin vs effective project and that console will surface both after the rollout.
carol: also update support playbook: how to interpret console fields and how to request attribution override.
dave: i'll add a lightweight audit log field `auth.project_resolution` that records the decision and reason (kept / no_claims / insufficient_perm). text-only field for now to avoid schema churn.
ben: thanks team — plan looks good. can we aim to flip console flag in 48h after canary metrics look clean?
alice: yes. I'll open the PR now for console flag + simple UI mock.
ben: please tag me and add a small smoke script to validate attribution for a few customers. :thumbsup:
carol: thanks — glad we can make attribution clearer quickly.
